content:
Requirement R20 (input): Command Handover. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to command a control handover of a UAV..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-20.1, F-20.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-20.<F>.1, Be-20.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-20.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R20 lets the pilot issue the actual handover *command* (execution phase) to transfer UAV control back to the UAV Pilot — the second phase after R19's request/acknowledgment, corresponding to UC 8.2 (command → break connection → hide status → confirm completion).

**Function candidates:**

**F-20.1 — Execute confirmed control transfer.** The function is to commit the handover: relinquish the pilot's active control link to the UAV so the UAV Pilot regains authority. Teleology = terminating the ownship's command relationship with that UAV. This is the direct analogue of R10 (establish control) inverted, and pairs with R19 (request) as R10 pairs with R09.

**F-20.2 — Guard against unintended relinquishment.** The function is to ensure the transfer of a live-controlled asset cannot be triggered accidentally — safeguarding an irreversible, safety-critical release of an airborne vehicle. Distinct goal: not "hand over" but "prevent mistaken hand over."

**F-20.3 — Reconcile the interface to the post-handover state.** The function is to bring the pilot's displayed context in line with reality once control is gone — retiring UAV status/control affordances so the pilot doesn't act on an asset no longer theirs (UC 8.1.16 hides status, 8.1.18 confirms completion). Goal = state coherence after release, not the release itself.

My recommendation: **F-20.1** as the primary — it's the requirement's stated intent (command the handover). F-20.3 is real but overlaps R13/R12 pane teardown and is arguably a Behaviour consequence of F-20.1 rather than a separate function. F-20.2 is a quality attribute better expressed as a confirm-gate in Behaviour (as in R09/R19) than a standalone function.

Which function do you want to close on?
Pretty much the same as R10, do the same thing we did to determine R19

For R19 I mirrored R09 (request phase). By that logic R20 should mirror **R10** (command/establish phase) inverted.

**Closing on F-20.1 — Execute confirmed control transfer.** Same pattern as R10 (establish control), reversed: R20 commands the *release* of the active control link. F-20.2 (guard) folds into the confirm-gate at Behaviour; F-20.3 (state teardown) is a downstream consequence, not the function.

**F-20.1 — Execute confirmed control transfer.**

Moving to Behaviour.

**Be-20.1.1 — Touch-only.** On the R19 handover-panel overlay (now in its second-phase COMMAND HANDOVER state after the request ack), pilot taps COMMAND HANDOVER, then taps a confirm affordance to pass the dual-input gate. System breaks the link and surfaces a connection-teardown progress indicator, then a completion confirmation. Mirror of R10's Touch path.

**Be-20.1.2 — Keyboard-only.** Same panel, driven by bezel OSS / UCP: OSS selects COMMAND HANDOVER, second discrete press (bezel or UCP) satisfies the confirm gate. Teardown progress + completion via the same indicator. Mirror of R10's keyboard path.

**Be-20.1.3 — Mixed.** Select via Touch, confirm via bezel (or vice versa) — the gate accepts any modality on either step, per the redundancy rule. Adds value as the realistic hands-occupied path (R10 precedent).

Same structure as R10: single second-phase state on the handover panel, dual-input press-and-confirm, progress indicator. Recommend carrying all three (they're the redundancy set, not alternatives).

Agree on the Behaviour set?

**Behaviour closed: Be-20.1.1 (Touch), Be-20.1.2 (Keyboard), Be-20.1.3 (Mixed) — dual-input press-and-confirm command handover with teardown-progress + completion feedback.**

Structure candidates (mirroring R10's extension-of-R09 approach):

**S-20.1.1 — Second-phase state on the reused R19 handover panel (R10-analogue).** Extend the R19 handover-panel overlay with a COMMAND HANDOVER phase that unlocks once the request-ack (R19/UC8.1) arrives. Elements: COMMAND HANDOVER control (Touch target + mapped bezel OSS), shared dual-input confirm gate (reused from R09/R19), and a connection-teardown progress indicator replacing R10's connection-progress indicator. On completion: R12 UAV status pane and R16 ISR pane retire (UC8.1.16 hide status), completion confirmation via R08 notification strip. UCP available for the confirm press.
→ Direct inverse of R10. Maximum reuse, single coherent handover panel spanning request→command.

**S-20.1.2 — Standalone COMMAND HANDOVER overlay.** A separate execution-phase overlay, distinct from the R19 request panel, invoked on ack. Same controls/gate/indicator but as its own layer.
→ Cleaner separation of request vs. command surfaces, but breaks the R09/R10/R19 single-panel lineage and adds an overlay for no functional gain.

**S-20.1.3 — Inline command action on the R12 UAV status pane.** Put COMMAND HANDOVER as a guarded action directly on the controlled-UAV status pane, so the command lives where the pilot is monitoring the asset. Confirm gate inline; pane self-retires on completion.
→ Contextually tight, but scatters handover across two surfaces (request on R19 panel, command on status pane) and duplicates the confirm gate.

Recommend **S-20.1.1** — it's the exact structural mirror of R10 and keeps request+command on one panel, consistent with how R19 mirrored R09.

Shared elements flagged: the dual-input confirm gate (R09/R10/R17/R19), R08 notification strip (completion), and R12/R16 pane retirement — all reused, not duplicated.

Which structure?

**Structure closed: S-20.1.1 — second-phase COMMAND HANDOVER state on the reused R19 handover panel**, with the dual-input confirm gate (R09/R10/R17/R19), teardown-progress indicator (inverse of R10's connection-progress), R08 completion confirmation, and R12/R16 pane retirement on completion.

R20 fully specified:
- **F-20.1** — Execute confirmed control transfer.
- **Be-20.1.1 / .2 / .3** — Touch / Keyboard / Mixed dual-input press-and-confirm with teardown-progress + completion feedback.
- **S-20.1.1** — Second-phase state on the R19 handover-panel overlay; shared confirm gate, teardown indicator, R08 strip, R12/R16 retirement.

Reuse flags: confirm gate, R08 strip, R12/R16 panes — all shared, not duplicated.

Ready for the next requirement, or want to close the set here.
